scenario: Every Monday, total the prior week's approved vendor bills in QuickBooks by vendor and cost center, compare against the budget tab in Google Sheets, and post a variance summary to the #ops-finance Slack channel.

When the procurement lead asks for an open-PO aging report, pull all open purchase orders from the procurement sheet, bucket them by days since issue (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+), and email the buckets with the top five oldest POs to the procurement lead.

Each morning, read inventory levels from the Google Sheets stock ledger, flag SKUs below their reorder point, rank them by days of cover remaining, and post the digest to the #warehouse Slack channel.

At month end, compare promised vs. actual delivery dates for every receipt logged in the receiving sheet, compute each vendor's on-time percentage, and append a scorecard row per vendor to the Vendor Scorecards sheet.

On the first of each month, count last month's facilities tickets in Freshdesk by building and category (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, janitorial), compute median resolution time, and email the summary to the facilities manager.

Quarterly, scan the IT asset register in Google Sheets for laptops and servers whose warranty expires within 90 days, group them by department, and post the list with counts to the #it-ops Slack channel.

When IT requests a license audit, compare seats purchased (from the SaaS subscriptions sheet) against active users exported per tool, compute utilization rates, and write a report doc listing tools below 70% utilization with estimated monthly waste.

Every two weeks, read the vendor contracts tracker for agreements with renewal or notice dates in the next 60 days, total their annual value by owner, and email each contract owner their upcoming renewals plus a consolidated list to the ops director.

Weekly, match Xero supplier invoices against PO amounts in the procurement sheet, list invoices exceeding their PO by more than the tolerance, and post the exceptions with total overage to #accounts-payable.

Monthly, pull Google Calendar bookings for all conference room resources, calculate booked hours vs. available business hours per room, and update the Room Utilization sheet with a ranked row per room.

Each Friday, read this week's orders from the order tracking sheet, compute the share shipped within the SLA by shipping tier (standard, expedited), and post the results with late-order IDs to the #fulfillment Slack channel.

Before the monthly safety meeting, read the employee certification tracker (forklift, first aid, hazmat), count expired and soon-to-expire certifications per site, and email the site leads a compliance status table.

Quarterly, check the vendor master sheet for certificates of insurance expiring or below required coverage limits, tally non-compliant vendors by risk tier, and post a summary to the #vendor-management Slack channel.
rule_hooks: minimum coverage by vendor risk tier

scenario: At month end, aggregate outbound shipment costs from the shipping log sheet by carrier and destination zone, compute average cost per package, and add a monthly row per carrier to the Carrier Costs sheet.

Every Thursday, read tasks from the Asana operations projects, count milestones completed, on track, and overdue per project, and post a status roll-up to the #ops-projects Slack channel tagging owners of overdue items.

After each cycle count, compare counted quantities in the count sheet against system quantities, compute unit and dollar variance per SKU and location, and email the inventory controller the items exceeding the variance threshold.
rule_hooks: variance threshold by item value class

scenario: Every Wednesday, read unpaid bills in QuickBooks due in the next seven days, total them by payment method and vendor, and email the controller a cash-requirements summary.
Each morning, count open IT helpdesk tickets in Zendesk by assigned group and priority, flag groups whose urgent backlog exceeds the limit, and post the snapshot to #it-helpdesk.

Every Monday, read upcoming start dates from the HR onboarding sheet for the next two weeks, check equipment orders and provisioning status in the IT tracker, and email the IT manager a readiness report counting ready, pending, and at-risk hires.
Monthly, aggregate employee travel expenses from the expense sheet by department, count line items exceeding per-diem or hotel caps, and post a departmental summary to the #finance-ops channel.
rule_hooks: per-diem and hotel caps by city

scenario: When a new price list arrives, compare unit prices in the latest supplier quote sheet against the current catalog sheet, compute percent changes per SKU, and email purchasing a ranked list of increases with the projected annual cost impact.

On receipt of monthly utility bills, total electricity, water, and gas costs per office from the bills logged in Xero, compare against the same month last year, and update the Facilities Costs sheet with variance columns.

Weekly, read customer returns from the Freshdesk returns queue, count them by product line and return reason, compute the return rate against units shipped from the orders sheet, and post the top reasons to #operations.
Every Tuesday, list DocuSign envelopes for vendor agreements and NDAs still awaiting signature, group them by days outstanding and internal sender, and email the legal ops coordinator the summary.

Monthly, read the company vehicle log for mileage and last service dates, determine which vehicles are due or overdue for maintenance, and post a count by location with the vehicle list to the #fleet Slack channel.
rule_hooks: service interval by mileage and months

scenario: Before the quarterly space planning meeting, compare headcount by team from the HR roster sheet against assigned desks per floor in the seating sheet, compute occupancy percentages, and write a capacity report doc highlighting floors above 90%.
Each afternoon, read pending purchase requests from the HubSpot custom object or request sheet, total value awaiting approval by approver, and Slack each approver their queue size and oldest request.
Monthly, pull Zoom Rooms meeting history, count meetings and total minutes per room, identify rooms with zero use, and append the results to the AV Equipment sheet for the facilities team.
Each morning, cross-reference open sales orders in Salesforce with backordered SKUs from the inventory sheet, total backordered revenue by account owner, and post the impact summary to #sales-ops.

Semiannually, compute each vendor's share of total spend per category from QuickBooks bill history, flag categories where one vendor exceeds the concentration limit, and email procurement a risk summary.

Ahead of the annual budget cycle, total next fiscal year's committed SaaS renewal costs from the subscriptions sheet by department, compare against the proposed IT budget tab, and write the shortfall per department into the Budget Review sheet.
rule_hooks: fiscal year boundaries and department allocations

scenario: Monthly, read freight damage claims from the claims tracker, total claimed vs. recovered amounts by carrier, compute recovery rates, and email logistics leadership the summary with claims open longer than 60 days.

Quarterly, compare the badge access list export against the active employee roster, count badges belonging to terminated employees or contractors past end date, and post the findings with totals per site to #security-ops.
Each evening, count inbound shipments and pallets received per dock door from the receiving log sheet, compare against the daily target, and add a row to the Receiving KPIs sheet.

Every Friday, read next week's field service visits from Google Calendar and Salesforce work orders, count visits per technician and region, flag technicians over capacity, and email the dispatch coordinator the schedule summary.
rule_hooks: max visits per technician per day

scenario: Monthly, aggregate office supply orders from the supplies request sheet by team, compare against each team's monthly allowance, and post the over-allowance teams and totals to #office-ops.

Weekly, read the vendor onboarding board in Trello, count vendors per stage (W-9 received, bank verified, security review, approved), list those stuck longer than the stage limit, and email the procurement manager the pipeline summary.

At month end, compare scheduled preventive maintenance tasks from the facilities calendar against completed work orders in the maintenance sheet, compute completion rates per site and equipment type, and write the results to the PM Compliance sheet.
Weekly, count Intercom conversations tagged as order status, delivery delay, or wrong item, compare with the previous week, and post the trend table with the largest increases to #customer-ops.

Before the annual compliance audit, check the audit evidence tracker sheet for each required control document, count received, missing, and outdated items by control owner, and email each owner their gaps along with an overall completion percentage to the compliance lead.
rule_hooks: required evidence list and freshness window

scenario: Every Thursday the IT ops lead asks for next week's on-call check. The agent reads the PagerDuty-style rotation in Google Calendar and the PTO tracker sheet, finds hours with no primary or backup engineer, and posts a gap table to #it-ops tagging the rotation owner.

Each month, ops finance requests a dead-stock report. The agent pulls SKU movement history from the inventory sheet, buckets SKUs with no sales or transfers in 90/180/365 days, totals the carrying value per bucket and warehouse, and writes the results to a 'Dead Stock' tab before emailing the supply chain director.
rule_hooks: aging buckets, write-down threshold at 365 days

scenario: At month close, the ops controller asks for budget vs actual. The agent reads ops cost-center actuals from QuickBooks and the annual budget sheet, computes the dollar and percent variance per GL line, and posts every line over tolerance to Slack, with the vendor driving it.
rule_hooks: ±10% or $5k variance tolerance per GL line

scenario: Each quarter, the CFO's office asks how capital projects are tracking. The agent matches capex-coded bills in Xero to the approved capex register sheet, computes the spend-to-date and remaining amount per project, and flags projects past 90% or over their approved amount in a summary doc.
rule_hooks: approved amount per project, 90%/100% alert levels

scenario: Each month, AP asks how much early-payment discount was captured or missed. The agent reads paid bills that carry 2/10 net 30 style terms in QuickBooks, compares each payment date to its discount window, and emails the AP manager the captured vs forfeited dollars by vendor.
rule_hooks: vendor payment terms, discount window days

scenario: Before the weekly payment run, AP requests a list of vendor credits not yet applied. The agent finds open vendor credit memos in Xero, ages them, matches each to open bills from the same vendor, and posts the credits that could offset this week's payments to #ap.
rule_hooks: credit memo age, same-vendor offset eligibility

scenario: Each week, the warehouse manager wants the mispick rate. The agent counts Zendesk tickets tagged wrong-item or missing-item against orders shipped from the order sheet, computes the error rate per picker zone, and updates the KPI row in the warehouse dashboard sheet.
rule_hooks: ticket tags mapped to error types, 99.5% accuracy target

scenario: Each quarter, facilities wants a lease outlook for offices and equipment. The agent reads the lease register sheet and the signed DocuSign envelopes, lists leases expiring within 12 months with their notice-by dates and monthly rent, and sends the list sorted by notice deadline to the facilities director.

Each month, building managers submit janitorial inspection forms to a Google Sheet. The agent averages the scores by building and by janitorial vendor, ranks the lowest-scoring areas, and posts a scorecard to #facilities that names each vendor below contract minimum.
rule_hooks: contract minimum score, scoring rubric per area

scenario: Each week, security wants a visitor log summary. The agent reads the visitor sign-in sheet and DocuSign NDA envelopes, counts visitors per site and host, flags lab-area visitors with no completed NDA, and emails the security lead.

Each quarter, the EHS coordinator asks which sites are behind on fire and evacuation drills. The agent compares the drill log sheet against each site's required drill frequency, and posts a table of overdue sites with their last drill date to Slack, tagging each site's safety warden.
rule_hooks: required drill frequency per site and jurisdiction

scenario: Every Monday, IT pulls the device inventory export into a sheet and asks for patch status. The agent computes the percent of devices on the current patch level per OS and department, lists devices more than 30 days behind, and posts the summary to #it-security.
rule_hooks: patch SLA by severity, 30-day lag threshold

scenario: Each week, IT asks which departed employees still have equipment out. The agent cross-references terminations in the HR sheet with assigned assets in the asset register, totals the unrecovered asset value per manager, and emails each manager the list for their team.
rule_hooks: return deadline after last day, asset value

scenario: Each month, the service desk lead wants to know which ticket categories get reopened. The agent reads Freshdesk tickets that were resolved and then reopened within 7 days, computes the reopen rate per category and agent, and adds a summary row to the service desk KPI sheet.

On the first of each month, IT wants upcoming domain and SSL certificate expirations. The agent reads the domain/cert inventory sheet, lists items expiring within 60 days along with their registrar, auto-renew status and owner, and posts the non-auto-renew items to #it-infra.

Each month, after the cloud bill lands, ops finance requests a chargeback. The agent reads the tagged cost export sheet, totals spend per team tag (untagged spend goes to its own line), compares each team to its budget, and emails each team lead their line.

Every Friday, the PMO asks for actual vs planned hours. The agent reads logged hours from the time-tracking sheet and the planned allocation in Asana, computes the variance per project and person, and posts any project over 15% to #pmo.

Before the Tuesday cross-team sync, the program manager wants blocked work. The agent pulls Jira issues marked blocked or with an unresolved 'is blocked by' link, groups them by blocking team, counts how many days each has been blocked, and posts a ranked list into the sync agenda doc.

Each Wednesday, the warehouse supervisor asks whether next week's shifts are staffed. The agent compares the shift schedule sheet against the minimum headcount per shift and role, then subtracts approved time-off. It posts every shift below minimum to #warehouse-leads.
rule_hooks: minimum headcount per shift and role

scenario: Every afternoon, receiving wants tomorrow's dock plan. The agent reads inbound delivery appointments from the dock Google Calendar and open POs from the PO sheet, counts appointments per door and hour, flags double-bookings and POs that arrive with no appointment, and posts the plan to #receiving.
rule_hooks: door capacity per hour, appointment-required carriers

scenario: Each week, compliance asks whether dangerous-goods shipments were documented. The agent filters outbound shipments of hazmat-flagged SKUs from the shipment log, checks the shared Drive folder for an SDS and shipper's declaration for each, and emails the compliance officer the missing items by shipment.
rule_hooks: hazmat SKU list, required document set

scenario: Each month, EHS wants an incident summary. The agent reads the safety incident form responses, counts incidents per site and type, separates OSHA-recordable cases, computes the incident rate using hours worked, and posts the summary to the EHS Slack channel.
rule_hooks: OSHA recordability criteria, rate per 200k hours

scenario: In early December, AP requests 1099 readiness. The agent totals YTD payments per vendor in QuickBooks, picks out the 1099-eligible vendors over $600, checks the vendor docs sheet for a W-9 on file, and emails AP the list of vendors still missing one, with their YTD totals.

Each quarter, internal audit asks for POs that skipped competitive bidding. The agent reads POs over the bid threshold from the PO sheet, checks whether each has three quotes or a sole-source justification attached, and writes the exceptions to an audit tab.

Each month, procurement wants to see maverick spend. The agent classifies QuickBooks bills and card transactions by category, compares the vendors against the preferred-vendor list, totals off-contract spend per department and category, and posts the top offenders to #procurement.

Five days before card statement close, finance asks for missing receipts. The agent finds purchasing-card transactions in the expense sheet that have no receipt attached, totals them per cardholder, and sends each cardholder a Slack DM with their list, plus a roll-up to the controller.
rule_hooks: receipt required above $25, statement close date

scenario: When an RFQ's response deadline passes, the buyer asks for a bid comparison. The agent reads vendor quote emails in Gmail, extracts unit price, lead time and payment terms for each line, ranks the vendors on total landed cost, and writes the comparison into a Google Doc linked to the RFQ.

Each week, procurement wants to know how much of each blanket PO has been used. The agent sums the invoices billed against each blanket PO in Xero, computes the percent consumed and the remaining balance, and posts the blankets over 80% or expiring within 30 days to #procurement.
rule_hooks: blanket PO cap and end date, 80% alert

scenario: Each month, quality asks for incoming inspection results by supplier. The agent reads receiving inspection logs from the QC sheet, computes defective parts per million per supplier, ranks the suppliers, and posts those over their quality agreement limit to Slack, tagging the supplier manager.
rule_hooks: PPM limit per supplier quality agreement

scenario: Every Monday, the inventory planner asks which lots are near expiry. The agent reads lot-tracked stock from the inventory sheet, lists lots expiring within the shelf-life window for each product class along with quantity and value, and emails the list sorted by expiry date to planning and sales ops.
rule_hooks: shelf-life window per product class, FEFO

scenario: Each day, the logistics coordinator asks about stuck inter-warehouse transfers. The agent reads transfer orders that have shipped but not been received from the transfers sheet, ages them against the expected lane transit time, and posts any transfer past its expected date to #logistics.

Each month, the ops director asks what rush shipping is costing. The agent filters expedited and overnight charges from the carrier invoices sheet, joins each to its order and requester, totals the cost by reason code and department, and sends the director a summary.

Each morning, the ecommerce ops lead wants a list of drop-ship orders that vendors haven't shipped. The agent reads open drop-ship orders from the order sheet and the tracking-number replies in Gmail, counts unshipped orders per vendor beyond the vendor's ship SLA, and emails a digest that ranks vendors by late orders.

Every Friday, the office manager wants a list of packages that haven't been picked up. The agent reads the mailroom intake sheet, finds packages unclaimed for more than 3 business days, counts them by recipient and floor, and posts a reminder list to #office.

Each quarter, facilities wants a list of equipment that costs more to keep fixing than to replace. The agent sums repair work-order costs per asset from the maintenance sheet, compares each total to the asset's replacement value in the asset register, and writes the assets over 50% into a capital request doc.

Each month, vendor management asks which service credits the company can claim. The agent reads the SLA breach records (uptime incidents, missed janitorial visits) from the vendor performance sheet, applies each contract's credit schedule, totals the credits owed per vendor, and emails the vendor manager.
rule_hooks: contract credit schedule per SLA tier

scenario: Each month, trade compliance asks for import duties paid. The agent reads customs broker invoices from Gmail and the entries sheet, totals duties and fees by HS code and country of origin, flags entries where the duty rate differs from the tariff reference sheet, and posts the results to a compliance tab.
rule_hooks: HS code tariff rates, country of origin

scenario: Each quarter, AP asks for a vendor master cleanup report. The agent scans QuickBooks vendors for likely duplicates (matching tax ID, normalized name, or remit address), totals the YTD spend split across each duplicate group, and writes the groups to a review sheet for the AP lead.

Every morning, the IT infra lead wants a backup status summary. The agent reads the overnight backup alert emails in Gmail, counts failed and missed jobs per system, lists any system with no successful backup in 48 hours, and posts the summary to #it-infra.

Each year in January, compliance asks which offsite record boxes can be destroyed. The agent reads the storage vendor's box inventory sheet, applies the retention schedule to each box's record type and date range, excludes boxes under legal hold, and emails a destruction-eligible list with box counts and storage fees saved.
rule_hooks: retention schedule per record type, legal hold list
